# yt001 thumbnail — a starting image and the prompt to finish it

**Nothing here was generated by an image model, and nothing here costs anything.** `thumb_base.png` and
`thumb_free_fallback.png` are Remotion stills (`remotion/src/yt/Thumb.tsx`, compositions `yt001-thumb` and
`yt001-thumb-base`) using the video's own globe, coastlines and blue dot. The prompt below is for *you* to run
in whichever image tool you use — per CLAUDE.md every image generation is charged, so that call is yours.

| File | What it is |
|:--|:--|
| `thumb_base.png` | **The image to start with.** 1920×1080. Real globe over India, four satellites, four beams meeting at the blue dot. Left 45% deliberately empty. No text. |
| `thumb_free_fallback.png` | The same image with the headline **GPS / NEEDS / EINSTEIN** set in code. Upload-ready if you want a thumbnail today and no face. |
| `composite.py` | After the model: keeps *its* left third, takes everything else from `thumb_base.png`, so the globe cannot drift. |

The globe, coastlines, Mumbai dot and cyan/blue/amber palette are the video's. The four satellites are drawn
**nearer and larger than scale** (an illustration, not a diagram) — the video's own constellation is the real one.

## Why this layout

* **One idea, readable at 168×94 px** (the mobile sidebar size — checked, also in greyscale): four lines, one dot.
  Every satellite beam ends on the same point, which is the whole video.
* **Three words, one colour accent.** Amber appears once, on the word that is the curiosity gap.
* **Nothing important bottom-right** — YouTube's duration badge sits there.
* **The left third is empty on purpose**: that is where the face goes, and where the headline goes.

## The prompt (attach `thumb_base.png`)

Works as an *edit* instruction for any model that takes an attached image (Gemini's image editor, ChatGPT's image
tool, Flux Kontext, Midjourney's Editor). Paste it as one block.

```
Use the attached image as the base for a YouTube thumbnail, 16:9, 1920x1080.

KEEP EXACTLY: the right 55% of the image — the glowing cyan-rimmed Earth centred on India, the four
satellites, the four cyan light beams that all meet at the single blue dot with the white outline.
Same positions, same colours, same sizes. Do not redraw, restyle, move or add to them.

ADD on the left 40%: a dramatic head-and-shoulders portrait of Albert Einstein in old age — wild white hair,
bushy moustache, rumpled collar, deep-set eyes, a faint knowing smirk, looking straight into the camera as if
he is the only one who knows the secret. The face fills roughly x 3–40% and y 2–55% of the frame; his hair and
shoulders may be cropped by the left edge, and his shoulders fall away into deep shadow below y 55%. Lit only from the right by the cyan glow of the Earth: a thin cyan
rim light on his hair, cheek and shoulder, the rest of his face falling into deep navy shadow.

Style: premium science-documentary key art — a photographic portrait graded to the palette, clean edge against
the background, very slight film grain. The background behind him is the same deep navy space as the base image,
continuing seamlessly to the left edge.

Palette ONLY: deep navy #040E1F, cyan #00D6F7, blue #51A4FF, bone white #E8E6E1. No other colours, no warm
tones (an amber headline will be added by hand later).

Leave the bottom 45% of the left half dark and empty (just shadow, no shoulders in bright light) — a headline goes there.
NO text, NO letters, NO numbers, NO logos, NO watermark, NO extra satellites, NO extra planets, NO lens flare.
```

**If the tool declines a named real person**, swap the second paragraph for:

```
ADD on the left 40%: a large side-profile silhouette of an elderly man with wild, cloud-like white hair and a
bushy moustache, filled with a faint star field and cyan constellation lines, rim-lit in cyan from the right.
```

(Or describe him without the name: "an elderly physicist, wild white hair, bushy moustache, rumpled collar".)

## Then, in this order

1. **Check the globe.** If the model nudged anything on the right, run
   `python3 -I composite.py generated.png` — it keeps the model's left third (x < 720, feathered out by x = 960)
   and takes everything else from `thumb_base.png`. Output: `thumb_composite.png`.
2. **Grade the face to the palette.** CLAUDE.md's rule for generated assets is *repair against the tokens, never ship
   as-is*: models get the geometry right and the colours wrong. Pull the skin toward bone `#E8E6E1`, the shadows
   toward navy `#040E1F`, keep the rim light cyan `#00D6F7`.
3. **Set the headline yourself** — image models mangle letters. Archivo Black (vendored in `remotion/public/fonts`),
   all caps, **three stacked lines**, bottom-left under the face, ~150 px at 1080p (y ≈ 600–1050, "NEEDS" is ~590 px
   wide), bone `#E8E6E1` with the last word in amber `#FFB020` and a soft dark shadow:

   | Headline | Claim it rests on | Read |
   |:--|:--|:--|
   | **GPS / NEEDS / HIM** *(HIM amber)* | the video's thesis — satellite clocks run 38.6 µs/day fast against the ground and GPS corrects it | best with the face: the face *is* the noun |
   | **GPS / NEEDS / EINSTEIN** *(amber)* | same | best with no face — this is `thumb_free_fallback.png`, already set at a size that fits |

   **Do not put "10 km a day", "11 km off" or any drift-per-day figure on it.** The video deliberately does not
   claim it (see `NOTES.md` — "Things deliberately NOT claimed"): 38.6 µs a day is computed, and light covers
   11.56 km in that time, but "GPS would drift 11 km a day" is a position claim the arithmetic does not make.
4. **Test it small.** Shrink to 168×94 and to greyscale. If you cannot read three words and find the dot, it is too busy.

## Two things to keep honest

* A **photo or likeness of Einstein** is an asset with its own provenance. A generated face carries no licence
  problem of its own, but if you use a real archival photo instead, check its licence first — I have not.
* The title and thumbnail must say the same thing. The video's title is *"How GPS finds you, and why it needs Einstein"*;
  every headline above is a shortened form of that.
